# BMS v0.0.3

Firmware **0.0.3+VC100** (`50c03fa`, `version_code` 100). Tag `v0.0.3` on `master-grok`, published 27 Nov 2026 (Europe/Vilnius); the earlier v0.0.3 was 0.0.3+VC97 (`eece3ff`), 0.0.3+VC96 (`e7ce2f5`) and 0.0.3+VC90 (`6144b8d`). This build fixes RS485 slaves that stayed offline.

## VC98–VC100

- VC98: watchdog heartbeat snapshot restore after a crash reboot (76 B packed snapshot); MQTT writes bounded to 5000 ms per write; `/diag` gains `mqtt_write_*` keys
- VC99: RS485 master waits 28791 us for the first reply byte (was 5 ms); failure back-off counted per slave instead of one shared counter
- VC100: a SLAVE on a board with RS485 and no slave CAN bus treats a stored `b_slave_com` None as RS485 in RAM only (NVS and `cfg_get` unchanged); every MASTER creates the `rs485_poll` task at boot and idles it when there are no slaves or the link is None; `/diag` gains `slave_link`. Wire format, baud, settings push and MQTT unchanged

## VC91–VC97

- VC91: dropped (the relay-control-via-web-UI row was Flasher-only; Flasher removed it in its VC57)
- VC92: default b_mqtt_contactor on when the NVS key is missing
- VC93: gate non-SE30 BMW iX PACK_SOC on E5CE ready, otherwise hold the last value
- VC94: one-decimal SoC for BMW iX (E5CE pptt) on web UI and BLE via soc_cpct (0.01 %); MQTT unchanged
- VC95: PSA V2 reads SOH once after boot (0x22 DC64) with retries at 5, 15 and 45 s, stored in PACK_SOH; /diag gains soh_boot_* keys
- VC96: CAN IDs shown as uppercase 0x-hex on serial, logs and /diag (lib/UTILS/can_id_fmt.h); cfg_set for b_ivt_id_base and b_i2c_addr accepts 0x, decimal or bare hex. Wire, NVS and MQTT unchanged
- VC97: copy CAN ID keys in /diag `psa2_tx_suppressed` and `can_dup_rx_ids` so /diag is valid JSON

## VC74–VC90

- VC74: PSA battery type rework + contactor/wake settings
- VC75: contactor control for PSA V1/V2, wake flag on all types
- VC76: match PSA V2 CAN contactor, wake and DTC clear to the eCMP schedule; keep TesterPresent and DTC read off eCMP UDS
- VC77: store every pack as one series cell count
- VC78: rename Waveshare RS485-CAN board label
- VC79: remove BMS web settings
- VC80: drive the negative contactor GPIO on BMW SE30
- VC81: drive the contactor sequence from b_ctc_ctrl
- VC82: replace split contactor controls with one b_ctc_type
- VC83: add CAN bus (stock BMS) as b_precharge 2
- VC84: reorder slave comm enum to 0 None, 1 RS485, 2 CAN
- VC85: reject CAN bus selectors the board cannot take
- VC86: default T-2CANFD inverter to CAN1, pack stays on CAN2
- VC87: carry b_cell_cap as 32-bit on the RS485 settings push
- VC88: send FAKE pack values on the Pylon live frames
- VC89: PSA V2 Clear DTC runs the reset sequence, add BLE reset_bms
- VC90: board_profile accepted only for the firmware image's own board(s)

## VC65–VC73

- VC65: BLE coredump_info and coredump_get
- VC66: BLE passkey pairing, bonding, and PIN reset
- VC67: show Read OTA data in a modal
- VC68: make grace and timeout timers safe across millis() rollover
- VC69: Resubscribe all MQTT topics after every connect
- VC70: Hold a BLE contactor close through every failsafe
- VC71: Honor the manual contactor hold on PSA 82 type 3
- VC72: Restyle the OTA page to match the dash
- VC73: Add an OTA button on the Status page

## Also in this release (after v0.0.2, through VC63)

- Drop the web Settings and Battery tabs; settings are BLE-only (`cfg_get` / `cfg_set` / `cfg_schema`)
- Publish cell and temperature CSV over MQTT (`cell_data`, `temp_data`); `rt` stays compact and adds module geometry
- Move the standalone CAN dash to OPF-DASH
- Give every web control a BLE command and drop the USB serial console
- Expose the cached pack DTC list on the BLE console (`dtc_list` / `DTC|` notify)
- VC53: remove Status action sections and their HTTP endpoints
- VC54: remove Status Health and flatten Device Overview
- VC55: remove BMS self-test and keep the OTA boot-health gate
- VC56: remove Dashboard Site summary and keep its values on Status
- VC57: add ap_hidden so the SoftAP can hide its SSID; drop the Hide SSID control from the Status page
- VC58: remove the Live data row from the Dashboard
- VC59: match application HTTP routes exactly
- VC60: build /diag snapshot off async_tcp; fix slim /health snapshot
- VC61: remove /health full duplicate and dead code
- VC62: task watchdog config + heartbeat snapshot in reboot log; fix task heartbeat ages
- VC63: coalesce soak NVS writes; label async_tcp heartbeat (not_watched, last feed on async_tcp_last_feed_age_ms)

BRIDGE.release_notes:
# BRIDGE v0.0.3

Firmware **0.0.3+VC52** (`2cbc835`, `version_code` 52). Tag `v0.0.3` on `master-grok`, retagged 27 Nov 2026 (Europe/Vilnius); earlier v0.0.3 tags were 0.0.3+VC51 (`4ddda59`), 0.0.3+VC48 (`8af90a2`), 0.0.3+VC47 (`12551a4`) and 0.0.3+VC43 (`ad9dc39`).

v0.0.3 moves all device settings to BLE (`cfg_schema` / `cfg_get` / `cfg_set`), leaves the web UI as a dashboard plus a read-only Status page, removes inverter auto-detect, hardens the firmware for 24/7 operation, adds BLE PIN pairing and a crash summary, and lists Sungrow SH6.0RS.

## Changes since v0.0.2 (0.0.2+VC34)

- **VC35:** web settings editors removed. Inverter and LoRa tabs are gone and Status-page actions (RS-485 tests, restarts, factory reset, SoftAP open/close, telemetry resume, smartmeter capture) move to BLE (`reboot`, `mqtt_restart`, `factory_reset`, `ap_open` / `ap_close`, `sta_drop`, `rs485_*`, `sm_cap`, `p1_key_set` / `p1_key_clear`, `p1_reboot`, `p1_uart_restart`). Every former web setting keeps its BLE key.
- **VC36:** Wi-Fi, SoftAP and MQTT (including TLS, the CA and the MQTT OTA host list) are BLE-only. The Settings tab, `POST /device`, `POST /api/security` and `GET /wifi/scan` are removed; `GET /device` stays for the Dashboard. The USB serial command console is removed (logs, `[BOOT]` line and panic text remain; esptool flashing is unchanged).
- **VC37:** Status drops the RS-485, Inverter Detect and Soft AP sections. Those were already BLE-only; the removed HTTP paths return `{"ok":false,"error":"not_found"}`.
- **VC38:** the hidden Profile selector and Status Warnings / Recent events are removed. Profile is BLE `cfg_set` only. `/diag`, `/health` and `/values` keep every key.
- **VC39:** inverter auto-detect removed. Boot loads the saved profile and does not probe the bus; `detect_*` BLE commands are unknown. Manual profile and slave selection, `rs485_info` and `rs485_scan` stay. Inverter writes are never auto-enabled; the write gate is set only by BLE `cfg_set` or MQTT `inv_writes`.
- **VC40:** Status is one plain read-only list.
- **VC41:** `ap_hidden` SoftAP setting (NVS, default 0), reported on `/diag` and `/health`, cleared by factory reset.
- **VC42:** unused dashboard WebSocket and dead web JS removed. MQTT TX buffer raised to 12288 so the ~8.3 KB heartbeat and diag publish. Health and diag buffers are reused, BLE notifies are paced, and `lora_rx` is on the task watchdog.
- **VC43:** the Storage and Battery confirm popup is replaced by an apply review page. Back (button, Esc, browser back) returns to the previous tab and keeps edits; Apply posts the same `/api/profile-command` batch.
- **VC44:** `/diag` reports `cdump_present` and, when a panic image is stored, a compact `cdump` summary (reason, cause, task, pc, backtrace, fw, ELF sha; max 288 B). Size map in `docs/SIZE_VC44.md`, LVGL trimmed, unused features compiled out on ESP32.
- **VC45:** BLE SMP passkey pairing with bonding (MITM, display-only, static passkey); TX/RX need an encrypted, authenticated link. New BLE keys `ble_auth` (default 1) and `ble_pin` (4-6 digits), `ble_pin_reset` over BLE (`confirm=1`) and USB, `auth:` command; `/diag` adds `ble_pin_set`, `ble_auth`, `ble_bonds`, `ble_encrypted`. Factory reset restores the default PIN and clears bonds. See `docs/BLE_PAIRING.md`.
- **VC46:** default BLE PIN is **123456**. A stored 1234 is removed once at boot and bonds are cleared.
- **VC47:** Sungrow SH6.0RS (profile `20`) is listed on the BLE `profile` schema (`0,1,10,11,20`, locked by a host test) and in the manuals; on profile 20 the Dashboard shows import / export / idle (max 5000 W), max export and max charge / discharge current. Review notes in `docs/SUNGROW_SH6RS.md`. No web profile picker (model selection stays in the Flasher and BLE app).
- **VC48:** the Atom S3R LCD page 7/7 (SETUP) shows the running firmware version and build (`FW 0.0.3+VC48`, `BLD 8af90a2`), from the same values as `/diag` and `/health`; the redundant ACTIVE SETUP heading is removed to make room.
- **VC49:** URL OTA pauses the HTTP listener (`opfWebServerQuiesce()` / `opfWebServerResume()`) around the blocking download so `/diag` and `/health` cannot hit async_tcp mid-transfer. ElegantOTA and BLE OTA keep the server. `/diag` and `/api/coredump/summary` include the running ELF SHA and `cdump_matches_build` so a dump from an older image is not read as a panic of this build.
- **VC50:** signed P1 LoRa commands (`uart_reset`, `reboot`, `radio_reinit`) can be queued from the web, BLE, or MQTT and transmitted in the uplink RX window. The key is a build flag (`P1_CMD_KEY_HEX`); without it the radio never leaves receive.
- **VC51:** `/update` is open without a password and restyled. ElegantOTA `/ota/start` and `/ota/upload` have auth cleared. URL OTA skips basic auth and keeps the CSRF, JSON, and confirm gates. `web_auth` still covers inverter and P1 writes.
- **VC52:** one shared logger stack buffer instead of a per-call buffer (about 0.5 KB less stack per task), comms and atom loops idle 10 ms instead of 1 ms (fewer idle wakeups), and the event-crumb ring is guarded by a spinlock to remove races.

Remaining write-capable web endpoints: `POST /api/profile-command` (Dashboard controls), `POST /api/ota-preflight`, `POST /api/ota-url` and ElegantOTA `/update`. Deye register 80 remains read-only. AUTOMATIC_MODE is unchanged.

## Hardware validation

- Atom S3R `.110` (Deye HV) already runs VC52 (`2cbc835`) (MQTT connected, subscriptions OK, minimum free heap about 85 KB after more than 5 hours; its fw_build label reads 4ddda59-dirty because that image was built just before the commit, from the same tree). `.236` (DTU base) has been unreachable since 24 Nov and was not retried for this retag. VC44/VC46/VC47 soak on `.110` since 20 Nov: free heap 88-97 KB, no new panic. Waveshare (ATOM_S3) and T-CAN485 (ESP32) images are built for the feed; T-CAN485 site flash is held until on-site rollback is possible.
- Sungrow SH6.0RS is code-reviewed and host-tested only; no Sungrow unit has been tested.
- T-CAN485 has no BLE and no serial commands, so its Wi-Fi/MQTT keys stay at the NVS values or the one-time build-flag seed.
- P1 LoRa downlink commands (VC50) are built in but not active until `P1_CMD_KEY_HEX` is set on both the Bridge and the P1 image.

## Build

Built locally from a clean `2cbc835` worktree with Arduino-ESP32 3.20016 (espressif32@6.7.0), without `platformio.local.ini` secrets, and published to the FEED with `scripts/publish_firmware_feed.py`.

P1.release_notes:
# P1 v0.0.3

**Frequency is 869.525 MHz (EU868 g3).** This is fw17: firmware **0.0.3+VC17** (`c94a98f`, `version_code` 17; the device's own version text reads `0.0.3+17`). Tag `v0.0.3` on `master-grok`, built from `c94a98f79e2473185ffc1ca3ef9becf2540e34dc`. Flash both images from this release together. The radio settings and uplink format are the same as v0.0.2.

- The P1 meter stays valid for 15 s (`P1_INVALID_AFTER_MS`), so a meter that sends every 10 s no longer flags every uplink as invalid. In v0.0.2 `dataInvalid` fired after 2 s.
- The transmitter clears USART1 overrun, framing, noise and parity errors (ORE/FE/NE/PE) on the live path. A stuck overrun used to stop reception.
- `recoverP1Uart` reinitializes the port after 30 s without an accepted telegram, then backs off to 60 s and 120 s. It does not reinit on top of a live meter.
- The telegram parser resyncs on `/` after a CR-only cut.
- Field diagnostics over SWD: `gFieldDiag` at `0x20002ffc` is now 75 words (`mdw 0x20002ffc 75`), with new `p1UartOre`, `p1UartFe`, `p1UartNe` and `p1UartPe` counters.
- LoRa downlink command to reset the P1 UART (`P1_UART`). Commands are accepted only when the transmitter is built with a command key. This FEED transmitter image is unkeyed, so commands are disabled.
- `FW_ITERATION_ID` is 17.

CONFIG_APP.release_notes:
# CONFIG_APP v0.0.3

- 0.0.3+109: Race Dash / PDM work since 0.0.1+104, including live input and formula values, pdm_caps field hiding, park-stop (wiperpark), bitrate labels that never show a raw number, and mid-transfer cancel for fs_put uploads (disconnect, no auto-reconnect). Android versionName is 0.0.3; versionCode is 2109 (Flutter arm64-v8a split-per-abi offset: 2*1000 + pubspec build 109), the same scheme as OptiPlex builds 107/108, so this package can replace the tablet's 2108 install. Arm64 split APK, signed with the OptiPlex debug key.

- 0.0.1+104: Cell count is the pack series total from `cell_count` / `b_cell_count`, shown as sent. `b_cells_editable` = 1 (or PSA Custom when that flag is absent on enum v4) is the only editable case, and Save writes `b_cell_count` as the total (1–108). Module counts are ignored. Live cells and temperature probes stay one flat list. Board profile 0 is labelled Waveshare CAN-RS485. The Type list keeps the pre-102 MEB, BMW, FAKE and Dash only entries, and a board without CAN-FD shows "MEB / BMW need a CAN-FD board".

- 0.0.1+103: BMS VC77 cells. Module count is gone from settings, and the live cell view is one flat bar chart (min blue, max amber, the rest green) with a table toggle. On `b_type_enum_v` >= 4, cell count is editable only for PSA Custom (or when cfg_get says so); PSA V1 shows 108 and V2/CMP show the pack count read-only.

- 0.0.1+102: BMS VC74 battery types. `cfg_get` `b_type_enum_v` >= 4 (or `version_code` >= 74 only when that key is missing) uses PSA V1 50/75, PSA V2 54/77/82, PSA CMP LFP and PSA Custom. Older firmware keeps the previous names and does not show the new fields. Contactor control (`b_ctc_ctrl`, GPIO/CAN) is PSA only. Wake (`b_wake`, Mute/Play) shows for every type except Dash only, and changing Type fills the wake default (V1/Custom/FAKE mute, V2/CMP/MEB/BMW play) without changing contactor control. Pack Test maps V1 → psa, V2 → psa82, CMP to no PSA50/75 commands, and Custom to listen-only.

- 0.0.1+86: BMS Controls Close and Open contactors on every BMS, each behind an Are you sure? warning. Close warns that it overrides a failsafe (cell under/over-voltage, temperature, latch) and uses a danger-style confirm. The commands are `contactor_close:confirm=1` and `contactor_open:confirm=1` (BMS VC70+ / VC71). A Manual override: ON (BLE) / OFF line is shown in Controls and compactly on BMS Live when `contactor_manual_override` is in telem; it is hidden on older firmware. OK/ERR replies stay in the snackbar. Race dash 0.1.12: `protocol` is an enum dropdown in CAN only when `cfg_schema` has a row for it (still hidden when it is only in `cfg_get`, so 0.1.7–0.1.11 stay unchanged). `redline_rpm` (1000–20000, default 7500) sits next to shift RPM. Demo mode notes that it runs a 12 s shift/redline sweep.

- 0.0.1+85: Settings fields and buttons share one style across the app. BMS settings used larger 48 px fields on tablets and phones and stretched them to the column width, so they no longer matched Bridge. Now every BMS, Bridge, Race dash, Screen and Local field is 28 px high with 3 px corners, the same 13 px text, the same field widths (104 / 216 / 440 px) and the same 18 px dropdown arrow. Bridge dropdowns no longer show 15 px text. Screen settings and Batch config text dropped from 15 px to 13 px, and their cards match the BMS and Bridge ones. The Device Name field uses the shared field text. Checkboxes are a 28 px box, and every button is 28 px high with 3 px corners.

- 0.0.1+84: Device Settings / View now opens as a full-screen page on tablets and phones, not a dialog or bottom sheet. This covers BMS, Bridge and Race dash View (all tabs: Settings, Wi-Fi, Debug, Controls, About, Update, BLE PIN) and the Screen (inverter) settings. The page has a back arrow at the top left. The back arrow and system Back both close it, and still ask before discarding unsaved edits. Nothing stays open behind the page.

- 0.0.1+83: Race dash firmware 0.1.8 (`c660a56`), still working with 0.1.7. After a successful Settings save the banner adds "Saving to dash memory - don't power off for 3 s." and About › Reboot dash is disabled with a countdown until 4 s after the last OK (the 0.1.8 flash write is debounced about 3 s). The BLE PIN block shows PIN: Default / PIN: Custom from `ble_pin_set` only on 0.1.8 or newer (from `status` or `fw_version`); 0.1.7 still shows no line. The BMS, Bridge and Screen PIN line uses the same wording. The 0.1.8 no-pages schema range `none` locks the start page with "No pages on the dash.", and `ERR|bad_value|no pages` on a page write shows the same note.

- 0.0.1+82: Race dash Settings never shows `protocol`, even if a later schema or `cfg_get` lists it. The start page is read-only, with a short "No pages on the dash." note, when `status` reports `pages=0` or the schema page range is empty (for example `0..-1`), and it is never written then. Race 0.1.7 always reports `ble_pin_set=1`, so the app still shows no Default / PIN set line.

- 0.0.1+81: Race dash Settings follows firmware 0.1.7 (`5795f3b`). The form is built from `cfg_schema` (Display, CAN, Wi-Fi, then any other keys), each value is checked against the schema before it is sent, and every change is a confirmed `cfg_set` (the firmware stores it at once; there is no separate save command). `OK|cfg_saved|…` now settles each write immediately instead of waiting 1.8 s (also BMS and Bridge). Read-only flags are never written. The BLE PIN block moved from About to Settings: Set PIN (4-6 digits, masked, confirm) and Reset PIN to 123456 (`cfg_set:ble_pin=clear`), then disconnect, remove the pairing and tap to pair again. There is no Default / PIN set line on Race because 0.1.7 always reports `ble_pin_set=1`, and no `ble_auth` switch because the schema range is `1`.

- 0.0.1+80: BMS VC66 and Bridge VC46 BLE PIN replies. Set and reset accept both `OK|cfg_saved|…` and `OK|ble_pin_reset|…`. `ERR|args|ble_pin` shows "PIN must be 4-6 digits", `ERR|error|nvs` shows "Device storage error (nvs)", `ERR|bad_request|…` shows its detail. Read-only flags (`ble_pin_set`, `password_set`, `ble_session`, and any schema `r` row) are never written. Changing Require pairing (`ble_auth`) now disconnects and removes the old pairing like a PIN change (BMS restarts BLE, Bridge reboots, Dash says reboot required), and the expected link drop is not shown as an error. Bridge `ERR|auth_no_pin|…` stops the old PIN prompt and shows the detail without retrying. The reply table and tests cover the new strings, and the Bridge `ble_drop` schema row parses.

- 0.0.1+79: The fleet default BLE PIN is now 123456 (passkey 123456) for BMS, Bridge, Dash/Screen and Race dash. The pairing dialog, Reset PIN to 123456, the reset confirms, the Wizard default-PIN warning and the Race schema fallback all use it. Setting 123456 counts as a reset to default (same confirm, `cfg_set:ble_pin=clear`), then the app disconnects and removes the old pairing. Reply formats are unchanged.

- 0.0.1+78: BLE SMP passkey pairing for BMS, Bridge, Screen and Race dash. When the first secured op (the TX notify subscribe) fails because the link is not encrypted or authenticated (GATT 5/8/12/15/137), the app says the default PIN is 1234 (passkey 001234), asks Android to bond (its passkey prompt), then subscribes again once. Bonded devices connect silently. `ERR|auth_required` also bonds first; the old `auth:<pin>` prompt is only a fallback when an already bonded device still refuses. Every device view has a BLE PIN block (BMS, Bridge and Race dash About; the Screen settings dialog): PIN set / Default from `ble_pin_set` (or `auth_status`), Set PIN (4 to 6 digits, entered twice, confirm, `cfg_set:ble_pin=<pin>`, never shown or logged) and Reset PIN to 1234 (confirm, `cfg_set:ble_pin=clear`). After an OK (`bonds_cleared=1` or `bonds=cleared`), or the link drop that follows, the app disconnects, removes the Android bond (plugin removeBond, then a native fallback, else a hint to forget the device in Bluetooth settings) and asks for a tap to pair again; nothing reconnects by itself. `ERR|bad_value|<detail>` shows the detail. The Require pairing switch (`ble_auth`) shows only when the schema accepts 0 and reports "Reboot required". Race dash Settings no longer shows `ble_auth` / `ble_pin`; the Bridge EV-tab PIN block moved to About. Local › USB has Reset BLE PIN (confirm, `ble_pin_reset`) and shows the reply line (Race `ok ble_pin_reset`, Dash `… ble PIN reset, bonds cleared`, Bridge `OK|ble_pin_reset|…`; `reset failed` / `ERR` = refused). `ERR|bad_pin` is shown like `ERR|bad_value`; `ble_unsupported` hides the PIN actions. The legacy PIN prompt accepts Race `OK|auth`, and after `ERR|auth_locked` it waits 60 s before another try. Reply strings for Race 0.1.6, Dash VC18 and Bridge VC45 are in one table in `lib/ble_pairing.dart`.

- 0.0.1+77: Race dash firmware 0.1.5. About sends the read-only `status` once when it opens and again on Reload (on the open link only) and shows it as the identity table (uptime as d/h/m/s, heap and PSRAM in KiB); `ERR|unknown_cmd` keeps the previous About. About › Maintenance has Reboot dash (`reboot:confirm=1`) behind a confirm. `password_set` / `ble_pin_set` are never form fields; the Wi-Fi password and BLE PIN boxes show Set / Not set as the placeholder, and an empty secret is never written. The page bounds come only from the runtime `cfg_schema` range (e.g. `0..1`).

- 0.0.1+76: OPF RACE DASH (ESP32-P4) support. Devices recognises manufacturer type 0x04 and `OPF-RACE-*` names as a Race dash, never a Screen (0x03). Its view has Settings, Update and About. Settings is built from `cfg_schema` (Display, CAN, Wi-Fi, BLE access, then any other schema keys), falling back to the `cfg_get` keys; secrets are masked and never prefilled, Save shows the "Write to …?" confirm, and reboot keys are written last. Update is the existing BLE OTA card (FEED product RACE; none published yet). About is the identity panel. Nothing is polled in the background; it connects only on a tap. Page/canmap `fs_*` transfer is not in the app yet.

- 0.0.1+75: BMS About › Maintenance can read a core dump on firmware 0.0.3+VC65. Info shows present, valid, size, firmware and status (and task, cause, pc, elf when a dump is present). Download reads 512-byte chunks, checks each CRC and the image CRC, then shares `coredump_<device>_<fw>_<time>.bin`. Older firmware hides the row. Erase stays a separate confirmed action and is never sent on its own.

- 0.0.1+74: Device Settings panels follow MANAGER (flat group boxes, primary tab mark, 28 px controls, radius 3). Local Wizard adds a BMS setup flow (BLE or USB, prefilled cfg, review, confirm, dry run, read-back). The Bridge wizard writes Solis discharge slots and Deye per-slot grid power. BMS Controls match the VC firmware commands, including live-UDS warnings and DTC pages.

- 0.0.1+73: BLE connects only on a tap on one device. No auto-reconnect after a drop (tap Retry), no bulk Connect paired/shown, no scan when Bluetooth turns on or the app resumes. Going to the background (paused/hidden/detached) stops scans, disconnects every BLE device and closes USB serial ports; inactive stops scans.

- 0.0.1+72: BMS and Bridge settings follow MANAGER VC11: cfg_schema forms, Hide SSID (ap_hidden), MANAGER tabs, Save confirm, loading state on device switch, About (identity + Maintenance) replaces Debug, BMS Controls. Version name back to 0.0.1 (v0.0.2 is retired).

- Build 62: BMS apply limits from DASH `6449e2b` (cell count 1–12, modules 1–36, capacity 0–65535, precharge delay 0–60000, temperatures, SoC hold 60–600). IVT CAN ID is shown on every Master. Bridge Settings follows the firmware registry at `2a54bf9`, including profile 20 SUNGROW and chunked `mqtt_ca`. Bridge dark theme is written as `classic`.

- Energy flow: inverter always centred. With P1 data, Grid sits above the inverter and a P1 box (net power, Hz) takes the old Grid spot. With V2C data, Load sits below the inverter and a V2C box takes the old Load spot. Otherwise the layout is unchanged.
- Every flow box (PV, Grid, P1, Battery, Load, Inverter, V2C) opens the same info dialog. The old Details view and the inline P1 LoRa card are removed; LoRa readings now live in the P1 dialog.
- V2C uses provisional `ev_*` keys (`lib/bridge_ev_keys.dart`) pending Bridge firmware.
- Settings field visibility/edit parity with DASH/Bridge web UI (74 BLE fields), battery enum v3, web-style section headers and buttons.

# OPF-CONFIG-APP (BLE sync)

- BLE BMS Battery settings mirrored to DASH web Battery UI (tip 0e27d0d): Pack → Slave → CAN → Inverter → Contactor → Shunt/IVT → Cell V/SoC → Temp → Current → Soft → Taper → Low SoC. The immutable folder `FLASHER/v0.0.3` and the git tag `v0.0.3` on `opelpanfan/OPF-FLASHER` are unchanged (both platforms there remain 0.0.2+VC95 from `6a925e2494777bb4e1a40eb6c3d8f2790873a812`).

Bundled Qt 6.8.3, esptool, and OpenOCD. Install with your package manager (`dpkg -i` or equivalent). Needs common system graphics and font libraries listed in the package Depends.
- **Windows:** `OPF-FLASHER-win-x64-VC104.exe` (the build number is in the file name; `OPF-FLASHER-win-x64.exe` is a copy of the newest build so old links keep working) — portable 7-Zip LZMA2 self-extractor, app version 0.0.2+VC104 from `opelpanfan/OPF-FLASHER` commit `c72c4cf09503ca2baa383d23583cf49775feab90` on `master-grok`. Cross-built on the OptiPlex (Qt 6.8.3, official MSVC kit, clang-cl). This Windows build has not been tested on a real Windows machine. Run the exe, extract the `OPF-FLASHER-qt-win64` folder, and start `OPF-FLASHER.exe` from that folder. Leave the Qt DLLs, the MSVC runtime, plugin folders (`tls/` included), and `tools/` next to the exe. esptool 5.5.0 and xPack OpenOCD 0.12.0-7 are bundled as Windows binaries. The package includes `tls/qschannelbackend.dll` and `tls/qcertonlybackend.dll`, which are required for HTTPS (the firmware feed index and downloads). MQTT in this app does not use TLS.

macOS is not included.

What changed in the Windows package since the v0.0.3 (VC95) feed build:

- TLS plugin folder is packaged and checked, and the app logs whether HTTPS will work at startup. A crash on Windows writes a minidump next to the session log.
- esptool 5 no longer starts a second verify run on the same COM port after a hard reset (ESP32-S3 native USB can get a new COM number). Serial errors use Windows wording (no "dialout") and mention CH340, CP210x, and ESP32-S3 drivers.
- CAN help names the vendor driver each backend needs on Windows, uses the Qt PEAK names (`usb1`, not `PCAN_USBBUS1`), and says listen-only still ACKs on vendor adapters. gs_usb / candleLight users are pointed at slcan firmware or a PCAN adapter.

It answers the PIN request with 123456 or the PIN you type in the app's own prompt, pairs several slaves one after another, removes a stale Windows bond and pairs again once, and if Windows reports a pairing already in progress for the device it unpairs, waits and retries once, then tells you to close the Settings dialog / remove the device / toggle Bluetooth. - Forget: Nearby devices that are paired show a Forget button (in the slot where Setup was; Setup is on the Connected card). It removes the Bluetooth pairing (Windows `UnpairAsync`, Linux BlueZ `RemoveDevice`) and the remembered-paired entry. The next Connect pairs again.

Linux is unchanged from the v0.0.3 (VC95) package.

# RACE v0.0.2

Version 0.0.2+VC12, commit f221cfea804e5e722623990af2b2aa1446562fc2 (master-grok, tag v0.0.2).

OPF Race Dash for the Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-Touch-LCD-7B (1024x600).

This folder replaces the earlier v0.0.2 package (0.0.2+VC11, 116fce7) at Benas's instruction. The annotated tag `v0.0.2` was moved to this commit.

## This release

- PDM mode & SCS200 integration (`0.0.2` VC1–VC12): Grayhill keypad (J1939 and CANopen 3KG1), read-only SCS200 telemetry, key 1–12 output commands, SCS analog inputs, `/pdm.json` rule evaluation with fail-safe CAN loss handling, PDM status and schema 2 setup over BLE, `pdm_scs_apply` ratings, CANBoard column frames, confirmed PDM bus bitrate change (`pdmbr` / `pdm_bus_baud`), output groups, and `pdmmodel`
- Keypad protocol (`pdmkpproto`, also `pdm_set:keypad.proto` and console `pdmkpproto`): `canopen` (default, current 3KG1 unit) or `j1939` (for the 3K012 units arriving later). CANopen node id is `pdmkpnode` / `keypad.sa`, default 10 (`0x0A`, 3KUM1331-1 Rev D §8 Table 1). Only a J1939 Grayhill locks the bus at 250 kbit/s. `pdm_bus_baud:grayhill_canopen:<250|500>:confirm=1` sends the documented LSS sequence (§9.3) and then tells you to power-cycle; nothing is sent without `confirm=1`
- Pages: dedicated portrait PDM status page (`07_pdm.json`, `orientation: portrait_cw`; firmware builds group and channel tiles from `pdmOutputs`), Keypad pages (`04_pdm_keypad.json`, `05_pdm_keypad_square.json`, `06_pdm_grayhill_single.json`) also portrait, with stage keys and centre-out shift bar, full-screen OPF BESS page (`03_bess.json`), and dash type selector (`Race` / `PDM` / `BESS`)
- Stability & settings: pre-rotated static labels into PSRAM images, GT911 I2C finite timeout + bus recovery, non-blocking USB console, slide watchdog, `diag` stall/hang command, Wi-Fi/BLE off at boot, on-screen settings popup (long-press 2 s or 3 s)

## Flash (esptool, USB, ESP32-P4)

Recommended: app only, at `0x10000`. This keeps NVS, otadata and LittleFS (`/pages`, `/canmap`, `/assets`).

    esptool --chip esp32p4 --baud 921600 write-flash 0x10000 esp32-p4.bin

OTA (HTTP `/fw` or BLE `ota_*`) also takes the app image only. Changed page JSONs (`data/pages/04..07`) can be pushed over USB console (`put` + `reload`) without erasing LittleFS.

Full flash (only if the bootloader or partition table must change). The P4 bootloader is at `0x2000`, not `0x0`:

    esptool --chip esp32p4 --baud 921600 write-flash \
      0x2000 bootloader.bin \
      0x8000 partitions.bin \
      0xe000 boot_app0.bin \
      0x10000 firmware.bin

The ESP32-C6 coprocessor is never flashed from this package.

# BRIDGE v0.0.3

Firmware **0.0.3+VC52** (`2cbc835`, `version_code` 52). Tag `v0.0.3` on `master-grok`, retagged 27 Nov 2026 (Europe/Vilnius); earlier v0.0.3 tags were 0.0.3+VC51 (`4ddda59`), 0.0.3+VC48 (`8af90a2`), 0.0.3+VC47 (`12551a4`) and 0.0.3+VC43 (`ad9dc39`).

v0.0.3 moves all device settings to BLE (`cfg_schema` / `cfg_get` / `cfg_set`), leaves the web UI as a dashboard plus a read-only Status page, removes inverter auto-detect, hardens the firmware for 24/7 operation, adds BLE PIN pairing and a crash summary, and lists Sungrow SH6.0RS.

## Changes since v0.0.2 (0.0.2+VC34)

- **VC35:** web settings editors removed. Inverter and LoRa tabs are gone and Status-page actions (RS-485 tests, restarts, factory reset, SoftAP open/close, telemetry resume, smartmeter capture) move to BLE (`reboot`, `mqtt_restart`, `factory_reset`, `ap_open` / `ap_close`, `sta_drop`, `rs485_*`, `sm_cap`, `p1_key_set` / `p1_key_clear`, `p1_reboot`, `p1_uart_restart`). Every former web setting keeps its BLE key.
- **VC36:** Wi-Fi, SoftAP and MQTT (including TLS, the CA and the MQTT OTA host list) are BLE-only. The Settings tab, `POST /device`, `POST /api/security` and `GET /wifi/scan` are removed; `GET /device` stays for the Dashboard. The USB serial command console is removed (logs, `[BOOT]` line and panic text remain; esptool flashing is unchanged).
- **VC37:** Status drops the RS-485, Inverter Detect and Soft AP sections. Those were already BLE-only; the removed HTTP paths return `{"ok":false,"error":"not_found"}`.
- **VC38:** the hidden Profile selector and Status Warnings / Recent events are removed. Profile is BLE `cfg_set` only. `/diag`, `/health` and `/values` keep every key.
- **VC39:** inverter auto-detect removed. Boot loads the saved profile and does not probe the bus; `detect_*` BLE commands are unknown. Manual profile and slave selection, `rs485_info` and `rs485_scan` stay. Inverter writes are never auto-enabled; the write gate is set only by BLE `cfg_set` or MQTT `inv_writes`.
- **VC40:** Status is one plain read-only list.
- **VC41:** `ap_hidden` SoftAP setting (NVS, default 0), reported on `/diag` and `/health`, cleared by factory reset.
- **VC42:** unused dashboard WebSocket and dead web JS removed. MQTT TX buffer raised to 12288 so the ~8.3 KB heartbeat and diag publish. Health and diag buffers are reused, BLE notifies are paced, and `lora_rx` is on the task watchdog.
- **VC43:** the Storage and Battery confirm popup is replaced by an apply review page. Back (button, Esc, browser back) returns to the previous tab and keeps edits; Apply posts the same `/api/profile-command` batch.
- **VC44:** `/diag` reports `cdump_present` and, when a panic image is stored, a compact `cdump` summary (reason, cause, task, pc, backtrace, fw, ELF sha; max 288 B). Size map in `docs/SIZE_VC44.md`, LVGL trimmed, unused features compiled out on ESP32.
- **VC45:** BLE SMP passkey pairing with bonding (MITM, display-only, static passkey); TX/RX need an encrypted, authenticated link. New BLE keys `ble_auth` (default 1) and `ble_pin` (4-6 digits), `ble_pin_reset` over BLE (`confirm=1`) and USB, `auth:` command; `/diag` adds `ble_pin_set`, `ble_auth`, `ble_bonds`, `ble_encrypted`. Factory reset restores the default PIN and clears bonds. See `docs/BLE_PAIRING.md`.
- **VC46:** default BLE PIN is **123456**. A stored 1234 is removed once at boot and bonds are cleared.
- **VC47:** Sungrow SH6.0RS (profile `20`) is listed on the BLE `profile` schema (`0,1,10,11,20`, locked by a host test) and in the manuals; on profile 20 the Dashboard shows import / export / idle (max 5000 W), max export and max charge / discharge current. Review notes in `docs/SUNGROW_SH6RS.md`. No web profile picker (model selection stays in the Flasher and BLE app).
- **VC48:** the Atom S3R LCD page 7/7 (SETUP) shows the running firmware version and build (`FW 0.0.3+VC48`, `BLD 8af90a2`), from the same values as `/diag` and `/health`; the redundant ACTIVE SETUP heading is removed to make room.
- **VC49:** URL OTA pauses the HTTP listener (`opfWebServerQuiesce()` / `opfWebServerResume()`) around the blocking download so `/diag` and `/health` cannot hit async_tcp mid-transfer. ElegantOTA and BLE OTA keep the server. `/diag` and `/api/coredump/summary` include the running ELF SHA and `cdump_matches_build` so a dump from an older image is not read as a panic of this build.
- **VC50:** signed P1 LoRa commands (`uart_reset`, `reboot`, `radio_reinit`) can be queued from the web, BLE, or MQTT and transmitted in the uplink RX window. The key is a build flag (`P1_CMD_KEY_HEX`); without it the radio never leaves receive.
- **VC51:** `/update` is open without a password and restyled. ElegantOTA `/ota/start` and `/ota/upload` have auth cleared. URL OTA skips basic auth and keeps the CSRF, JSON, and confirm gates. `web_auth` still covers inverter and P1 writes.
- **VC52:** one shared logger stack buffer instead of a per-call buffer (about 0.5 KB less stack per task), comms and atom loops idle 10 ms instead of 1 ms (fewer idle wakeups), and the event-crumb ring is guarded by a spinlock to remove races.

Remaining write-capable web endpoints: `POST /api/profile-command` (Dashboard controls), `POST /api/ota-preflight`, `POST /api/ota-url` and ElegantOTA `/update`. Deye register 80 remains read-only. AUTOMATIC_MODE is unchanged.

## Hardware validation

- Atom S3R `.110` (Deye HV) already runs VC52 (`2cbc835`) (MQTT connected, subscriptions OK, minimum free heap about 85 KB after more than 5 hours; its fw_build label reads 4ddda59-dirty because that image was built just before the commit, from the same tree). `.236` (DTU base) has been unreachable since 24 Nov and was not retried for this retag. VC44/VC46/VC47 soak on `.110` since 20 Nov: free heap 88-97 KB, no new panic. Waveshare (ATOM_S3) and T-CAN485 (ESP32) images are built for the feed; T-CAN485 site flash is held until on-site rollback is possible.
- Sungrow SH6.0RS is code-reviewed and host-tested only; no Sungrow unit has been tested.
- T-CAN485 has no BLE and no serial commands, so its Wi-Fi/MQTT keys stay at the NVS values or the one-time build-flag seed.
- P1 LoRa downlink commands (VC50) are built in but not active until `P1_CMD_KEY_HEX` is set on both the Bridge and the P1 image.

## Build

Built locally from a clean `2cbc835` worktree with Arduino-ESP32 3.20016 (espressif32@6.7.0), without `platformio.local.ini` secrets, and published to the FEED with `scripts/publish_firmware_feed.py`.

# OPF-FLASHER latest (Linux 0.0.2+VC95, Windows 0.0.2+VC104)

`FLASHER/latest` is a mixed package. The Linux deb is still the tagged v0.0.3 build. The Windows portable exe is a newer desktop build. The immutable folder `FLASHER/v0.0.3` and the git tag `v0.0.3` on `opelpanfan/OPF-FLASHER` are unchanged (both platforms there remain 0.0.2+VC95 from `6a925e2494777bb4e1a40eb6c3d8f2790873a812`).

- **Linux:** `OPF-FLASHER-linux-amd64.deb` — amd64 package 0.0.2+VC95, built on the OptiPlex from `opelpanfan/OPF-FLASHER` commit `6a925e2494777bb4e1a40eb6c3d8f2790873a812` on `master-grok` (git tag `v0.0.3`). Bundled Qt 6.8.3, esptool, and OpenOCD. Install with your package manager (`dpkg -i` or equivalent). Needs common system graphics and font libraries listed in the package Depends.
- **Windows:** `OPF-FLASHER-win-x64-VC104.exe` (the build number is in the file name; `OPF-FLASHER-win-x64.exe` is a copy of the newest build so old links keep working) — portable 7-Zip LZMA2 self-extractor, app version 0.0.2+VC104 from `opelpanfan/OPF-FLASHER` commit `c72c4cf09503ca2baa383d23583cf49775feab90` on `master-grok`. Cross-built on the OptiPlex (Qt 6.8.3, official MSVC kit, clang-cl). This Windows build has not been tested on a real Windows machine. Run the exe, extract the `OPF-FLASHER-qt-win64` folder, and start `OPF-FLASHER.exe` from that folder. Leave the Qt DLLs, the MSVC runtime, plugin folders (`tls/` included), and `tools/` next to the exe. esptool 5.5.0 and xPack OpenOCD 0.12.0-7 are bundled as Windows binaries. The package includes `tls/qschannelbackend.dll` and `tls/qcertonlybackend.dll`, which are required for HTTPS (the firmware feed index and downloads). MQTT in this app does not use TLS.

macOS is not included.

What changed in the Windows package since the v0.0.3 (VC95) feed build:

- TLS plugin folder is packaged and checked, and the app logs whether HTTPS will work at startup. A crash on Windows writes a minidump next to the session log.
- esptool 5 no longer starts a second verify run on the same COM port after a hard reset (ESP32-S3 native USB can get a new COM number). Serial errors use Windows wording (no "dialout") and mention CH340, CP210x, and ESP32-S3 drivers.
- CAN help names the vendor driver each backend needs on Windows, uses the Qt PEAK names (`usb1`, not `PCAN_USBBUS1`), and says listen-only still ACKs on vendor adapters. gs_usb / candleLight users are pointed at slcan firmware or a PCAN adapter.
- BLE pairing on Windows: the app pairs each device itself before any GATT access (WinRT custom pairing with ProvidePin / ConfirmPinMatch / ConfirmOnly / DisplayPin, protection level EncryptionAndAuthentication; works with LE Secure Connections and legacy pairing). It answers the PIN request with 123456 or the PIN you type in the app's own prompt, pairs several slaves one after another, removes a stale Windows bond and pairs again once, and if Windows reports a pairing already in progress for the device it unpairs, waits and retries once, then tells you to close the Settings dialog / remove the device / toggle Bluetooth. A link the device drops right after connecting is reported as a failed connect, not as Ready. The "already connected on this computer" check is skipped on Windows. BLE OTA logs the MTU and uses acknowledged writes when Windows reports 23 or does not report one.
- Forget: Nearby devices that are paired show a Forget button (in the slot where Setup was; Setup is on the Connected card). It removes the Bluetooth pairing (Windows `UnpairAsync`, Linux BlueZ `RemoveDevice`) and the remembered-paired entry. The next Connect pairs again.

Linux is unchanged from the v0.0.3 (VC95) package.

- PDM mode & SCS200 integration (`0.0.2` VC1–VC12): Grayhill keypad (J1939 and CANopen 3KG1), read-only SCS200 telemetry, key 1–12 output commands, SCS analog inputs, `/pdm.json` rule evaluation with fail-safe CAN loss handling, PDM status and schema 2 setup over BLE, `pdm_scs_apply` ratings, CANBoard column frames, confirmed PDM bus bitrate change (`pdmbr` / `pdm_bus_baud`), output groups, and `pdmmodel`
- Keypad protocol (`pdmkpproto`, also `pdm_set:keypad.proto` and console `pdmkpproto`): `canopen` (default, current 3KG1 unit) or `j1939` (for the 3K012 units arriving later). CANopen node id is `pdmkpnode` / `keypad.sa`, default 10 (`0x0A`, 3KUM1331-1 Rev D §8 Table 1). Only a J1939 Grayhill locks the bus at 250 kbit/s. `pdm_bus_baud:grayhill_canopen:<250|500>:confirm=1` sends the documented LSS sequence (§9.3) and then tells you to power-cycle; nothing is sent without `confirm=1`
- Pages: dedicated portrait PDM status page (`07_pdm.json`, `orientation: portrait_cw`; firmware builds group and channel tiles from `pdmOutputs`), Keypad pages (`04_pdm_keypad.json`, `05_pdm_keypad_square.json`, `06_pdm_grayhill_single.json`) also portrait, with stage keys and centre-out shift bar, full-screen OPF BESS page (`03_bess.json`), and dash type selector (`Race` / `PDM` / `BESS`)
- Stability & settings: pre-rotated static labels into PSRAM images, GT911 I2C finite timeout + bus recovery, non-blocking USB console, slide watchdog, `diag` stall/hang command, Wi-Fi/BLE off at boot, on-screen settings popup (long-press 2 s or 3 s)

## Flash (esptool, USB, ESP32-P4)

Recommended: app only, at `0x10000`. This keeps NVS, otadata and LittleFS (`/pages`, `/canmap`, `/assets`).

    esptool --chip esp32p4 --baud 921600 write-flash 0x10000 esp32-p4.bin

OTA (HTTP `/fw` or BLE `ota_*`) also takes the app image only. Changed page JSONs (`data/pages/04..07`) can be pushed over USB console (`put` + `reload`) without erasing LittleFS.

    esptool --chip esp32p4 --baud 921600 write-flash \
      0x2000 bootloader.bin \
      0x8000 partitions.bin \
      0xe000 boot_app0.bin \
      0x10000 firmware.bin

The ESP32-C6 coprocessor is never flashed from this package.

The firmware itself reports `fw_version=0.0.2` (`VC12`, `version_code=12` in feed metadata: `0.0.2+VC12`).
